Getting started › Your first web app

Your first web app

You will build a small ASP.NET Core site whose script is written in TypeScript, and see it served as JavaScript. You need the .NET 10 SDK and a terminal. No Node.

1. Create the project

bash 
dotnet new web -n Hello
cd Hello

2. Add the packages

bash 
dotnet add package Extrode.Pare.Build
dotnet add package Extrode.Pare.AspNetCore

Open Hello.csproj and mark the build package private. This keeps the build step out of any project that references yours:

XML 
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Extrode.Pare.Build" Version="0.7.1" PrivateAssets="all" />
  <PackageReference Include="Extrode.Pare.AspNetCore" Version="0.7.1" />
</ItemGroup>

Use the version dotnet add package wrote for you; 0.7.1 here is only an example.

What each does:

  • Extrode.Pare.Build strips every wwwroot/**/*.ts when you run dotnet build.
  • Extrode.Pare.AspNetCore strips again when you save a .ts while dotnet watch runs, so you see the change without a rebuild.

3. Serve static files

Replace Program.cs with:

C# 
using Extrode.Pare.AspNetCore;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.AddPareDevelopment();   // does nothing outside Development
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseDefaultFiles();          // "/" serves index.html
app.UseRouting();
app.MapStaticAssets();          // serves what the build registered, including Pare's output

app.Run();

4. Write some TypeScript

Create wwwroot/index.html:

HTML 
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Hello, Pare</title>
  <script type="module" src="/js/app.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <h1 id="greeting"></h1>
</body>
</html>

The page asks for /js/app.js. You will only write app.ts. Create wwwroot/js/app.ts:

ts 
interface Person {
  name: string;
}

function greet(person: Person): string {
  return `Hello, ${person.name}!`;
}

const heading = document.querySelector("#greeting")!;
heading.textContent = greet({ name: "Pare" });

5. Build and run

bash 
dotnet build

Look at what the build made:

text 
obj/Debug/net10.0/pare/js/app.js

That is your script with the types gone. Open it and compare it with app.ts: same lines, same columns.

bash 
dotnet run

Open the address it prints. You should see "Hello, Pare!". Your browser asked for /js/app.js and the build had already registered the stripped file as that URL.

6. Edit and watch it reload

Stop the app and run it with hot reload:

bash 
dotnet watch

Change "Pare" in app.ts to your own name and save. The page reloads with the new text and the app does not restart.

dotnet watch runs no build when only a .ts changes. Without AddPareDevelopment() the .js would go stale. That one line is what keeps it fresh.

7. See an error

Add this to the end of app.ts, after a blank line:

ts 
enum Color { Red, Green }

Build again:

text 
wwwroot/js/app.ts(12,1): error PARE100: 'enum' generates runtime code and cannot be erased
(use a 'const' object with 'as const' instead of 'enum')

It reads like a C# compiler error and points at the line. Under dotnet watch the same message appears in the log and the old .js keeps being served. Replace the enum with the suggestion and it builds again. All the codes are in Error codes.

8. Publish

bash 
dotnet publish -c Release

The published site holds app.js with .br and .gz copies. The .ts source is not published. Set PareKeepSources=true if you want it there.
